files: A Python repo with uncommitted work: a `parse_date` helper moved from `loader.py` to a new `dates.py` with no behavior change, and in the same `loader.py` a fix that filters out blank lines before calling it
expected_behavior: Runs git status and git diff before staging anything
Makes the refactor commit first, with a subject starting `refactor(` that names the moved helper
Makes a second commit for the fix, with a subject starting `fix(`
Stages each commit's files by name, with no git add . or git add -A
Writes a body only where the subject can't say why and the work shows the reason, and never restates the diff
When loader.py holds both concerns, the refactor commit holds only the extraction and the fix commit holds only the blank-line filter
Gives each subject as imperative and lowercase, with no trailing period and 72 characters or fewer
Reports both commit hashes and subjects, and pushes nothing

files: A repo with uncommitted changes: a rounding bug fix in `billing/rounding.py` and a typo fix in `README.md`
expected_behavior: Makes one commit for billing/rounding.py and a separate docs commit for README.md
Stages README.md by name, not with git add -A
Gives the docs commit no body, since its subject says it all

query: Also commit the new test in its own commit.
files: The repo after the two commits from the previous scenario, plus an uncommitted `tests/test_rounding.py` that covers the fix
expected_behavior: Stages only tests/test_rounding.py, by name
Commits it with a subject starting `test(`
Leaves the two earlier commits unchanged

files: Uncommitted changes: a feature in `api.py`, and a `notes.txt` of scratch text with no clear purpose
expected_behavior: Commits the feature in api.py
Asks which commit notes.txt belongs to, and stages nothing for it

query: Commit my changes. The last commit message was sloppy.
files: A repo with uncommitted changes to src/parse.py that add a guard for empty input, and one unpushed commit 'wip' on top of main
expected_behavior: Makes a new commit for the changes and leaves the 'wip' commit as it is
Doesn't amend, rebase or reset the 'wip' commit, since the user didn't ask for that

files: A repo whose working tree is clean
expected_behavior: Says there is nothing to commit
Makes no commit, not even an empty one

files: Uncommitted work that adds a `mul` function to `calc.py`, a test for it in `tests/test_calc.py`, and a README section describing it: one purpose, with tests and docs
expected_behavior: Makes one commit that holds calc.py, tests/test_calc.py and README.md together
Gives that commit a subject starting `feat(`, not a separate `test(` or `docs(` commit
Stages each file by name, with no git add . or git add -A

files: Uncommitted change to `api.py` that deletes the public function `load_legacy`, which callers must now replace with `load`
expected_behavior: Makes one commit for api.py
Marks the subject as breaking with `!` before the colon
Adds a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer after a blank line that says what breaks and what to use instead

files: Uncommitted changes: `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock` bump `httpx` to a newer version, `.github/workflows/test.yml` adds Python 3.13 to the test matrix, and `src/report.py` is reformatted by ruff with no code change
expected_behavior: Makes three commits, one per change
Gives the dependency bump a subject starting `build(`, the workflow change one starting `ci(` and the reformat one starting `style(`
Uses `chore(` for none of them
